desc:
A React Native app audit and code review shows what is slow, risky or likely to fail store checks, ranked by effort and impact. Ecom Swift LLC reads your repository, runs the app on iOS and Android, and sends a written report you can act on straight away.

## What is a React Native app audit?

A React Native audit is a structured review of an existing app's code, speed, stability and store readiness. A reviewer reads the project, runs it on both platforms and records every problem found. The result is a written report, not a rewrite.

The report ranks findings, so a small fix that removes a crash sits above a large refactor that only tidies style. That ranking is what makes the audit useful to someone who is not a developer.

## Why do apps need a code review before they grow?

Most app problems start small. A library that is no longer maintained, a list that renders every row at once, a screen that stores data in three places: none of these hurt on day one. They hurt when the user count grows, when a new iOS release arrives or when a second developer joins and cannot follow the code.

An outside review finds these issues while they are still cheap to fix. It also gives you an independent view if you inherited the app from a previous developer or agency and are unsure what you actually own.

## How an audit affects users and costs

Users never see your code, but they feel its effects. Slow startup, janky lists and unexpected crashes lead to low ratings and uninstalls. A weak dependency can also expose user data or stop the build from compiling after an update.

An audit helps by pointing money at the right place. Instead of paying for a full rewrite or guessing which bug matters, you get an ordered list. Each item says what is wrong, why it matters and roughly how hard it is to fix. Results still depend on how quickly the fixes are made.

## What a thorough audit covers

- Project structure, folder layout and naming that a new developer can follow.
- Dependency health: outdated, unmaintained or duplicated libraries.
- Security basics such as keys stored in the app, unsafe storage and unencrypted calls.
- Startup time and list scrolling behavior on a mid-range phone.
- Crash and error logs from your reporting tool, if you have one.
- Store requirements for both Apple and Google that could block an update.
- State management and data flow, including places where state is repeated.
- Accessibility on key screens: text size, contrast and labels for screen readers.
- Navigation, deep links and handling of the Android back button.
- A fix roadmap with time estimates for the larger packages.

## What we do

You send read access to the repository and, if available, crash reports and store notices. We read the code before running anything, so we know what the app is meant to do.

Then we run the app on both platforms, measure the slow spots and scan the dependencies. The Basic package delivers a written review with the top ten findings ranked. Standard adds speed tests, log review, a store check and a thirty minute call. Premium adds accessibility, architecture review, a roadmap and a few sample fixes that show how the work should be done.

We do not change your code during the audit unless a sample fix is part of your package.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share the repository and the latest store release notes.
- Tell us what worries you most: crashes, speed, a failed review or an unclear codebase.
- Include crash reports and user complaints if you have them.
- Read the top findings first and fix them before starting new features.
- Ask for a re-check after the fixes are done.

**Avoid:**
- Waiting for a store rejection before reviewing the app.
- Treating every finding as equally urgent.
- Sending the audit to a freelancer without a plan to act on it.
- Updating many libraries at once without testing between changes.
- Sharing passwords or private keys with anyone, including us.

## Who this service is for

An owner who bought or inherited an app and wants to know what shape it is in. A startup preparing for a larger launch or for investor questions about technical quality. A small team with a growing list of complaints and no clear idea which bug to fix first.

## What we need from you

A link to the repository with read access, given as a collaborator on your code host. If you have them, add crash reports, analytics screenshots and any store messages about policy or review. We never need your passwords or signing keys. Tell us your main concern in one short note, and we will confirm the scope before starting.
